blocks.explanation:
\(e^x\,dx = d(e^x)\), so substitute \(t = e^x\).
Plan: \(\int \tan^{-1}t\,dt\) by parts with \(\tan^{-1}t\cdot 1\).
steps:
Given: \(\int e^x\tan^{-1}(e^x)\,dx\).
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: substitute \(t = e^x\); then \(\int \tan^{-1}t\cdot 1\,dt\) by parts.

Substitute
\[t = e^x \Rightarrow dt = e^x\,dx\]
\[= \int \tan^{-1}t\,dt\]
Why: \(e^x\,dx = dt\).

Parts with \(\tan^{-1}t\cdot 1\)
\[= t\tan^{-1}t - \int t\cdot\dfrac{1}{1+t^2}\,dt\]
Why: \(\frac{d}{dt}\tan^{-1}t = \frac{1}{1+t^2}\), \(\int 1\,dt = t\).

Log integral
\[\int \dfrac{t}{1+t^2}\,dt = \dfrac{1}{2}\int \dfrac{2t}{1+t^2}\,dt\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(1+t^2)\]
Why: \(2t\) is the derivative of \(1 + t^2\).

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(\ldots) = e^x\tan^{-1}(e^x) + \dfrac{e^{2x}}{1+e^{2x}} - \dfrac{e^{2x}}{1+e^{2x}}\]
\[= e^x\tan^{-1}(e^x)\]
Why: the two fractions cancel.
